reader.requirement: At 1985, UNSTRING examines identifier-1 from the POINTER position (or position 1), up to a delimiter when DELIMITED BY is written or else for the size of the current receiving area (one less for a separate sign), stopping at the end of identifier-1; moves the examined characters as an alphanumeric item by MOVE rules into the receiver (alphabetic, alphanumeric or numeric DISPLAY), the delimiter (space fill at end of data) into DELIMITER IN and the count into COUNT IN, continues after the delimiter or the last character transferred, and repeats until the sender is exhausted or the receivers run out.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.UnstringZeroLengthSenderTerminates (2002+): the zero-length-sender guard; 1985 takes no guard and lets GR17a decide, which does not touch any GR13 step
Constructs.UnstringSenderReferenceModified2002: a reference-modified identifier-1 is refused at 85 (COBOL0900, §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR7) and accepted from 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a reference-modified sender is refused (SR7) and the 2002+ zero-length-sender termination is absent; the GR13 transfer steps a to g run the same code at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb979_unstring_receiver_size covers the no-DELIMITED size rule; POINTER start, DELIMITER IN and COUNT IN, end-of-sender DELIMITER IN space fill, ALL, OR, JUSTIFIED, numeric/scaled/alphabetic receivers, the separate-sign 'one less' and a variable-length sender are not in the witness

probes.expected: 13a POINTER start; 13b delimiter or size (digits; leading separate sign examines 3 of 4); 13c MOVE rules (JUSTIFIED, scaled 789 -> 9.00, alphabetic); 13d one ALL occurrence and space fill at end of data; 13e counts; 13g an area not reached keeps its contents
numeric receivers, contiguous delimiters zero fill (GR9); two-character identifier delimiter into DELIMITER IN; ODO group sender at current extent 5; trailing separate sign examines 3

reader.notes: EmitUnstring unrolls one UnstringExtract per receiver, the size from ReceivingStore.ExaminationSize (digits for numeric, so a separate sign is the one less) and the store through the bound MOVE; every GR13 step matched the 1985 text in the probes. DISPLAY of the PIC 9V99 receiver prints 9.00 (an inserted point), which is DISPLAY's own behaviour and not this rule; the stored value 9.00 is the MOVE rule's.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85: r3_unstring.cob (runs/r3_unstring-001): F1 'UNSTRING S1 DELIMITED BY "," INTO IX TR(IX) TR(IX)' with IX=1 printed IX=3 [BBB............] = the subscript evaluated once at the start (§1985:IV.4.3.8, no UNSTRING rule says otherwise) and the second receiver overwrites TR(1); D1 delimiter identifier PIC X(3) VALUE ',' is the whole 3-character content: [AB   ][CD,EF][     ] (GR11); D2 DELIMITED BY SPACE with contiguous spaces space-fills the receiver: [AB   ][     ][CD   ] (GR8, GR9); D3 ALL SPACE: one occurrence into DELIMITER IN, COUNT IN 2 excludes delimiters; D4 DELIMITED BY ZERO is the character '0': [12   ][3    ][     ]; G1 group receiver with no DELIMITED BY examines the group size 4: [XY12][ZZ   ]; J1 two-character delimiter into a 1-character and a 4-character JUSTIFIED RIGHT DELIMITER IN: [-] and [  -*]. r3_unstring_b.cob (runs/r3_unstring_b-001): inside-ODO group receiver examines its maximum 6 (GN=4 from data, R1 [FGHIJK]); outside-ODO group receiver examines its current 4 ([4ABC   ][DEFGHI]); reference-modified receiver R2(2:3) examines 3 ([.4AB..]); DELIMITED into S9(4) and 9(2)V9: +2345 and 07.0 (unsigned-integer MOVE rule). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8  the text is in the clause'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR8'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR11'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR13b'.
refuter.corrected: Not this rule: DISPLAY of an unedited PIC 9(2)V9 item prints 07.0 with an inserted point (the reader saw the same with 9V99); that is the DISPLAY statement's behaviour and worth its own check against the 1985 DISPLAY rules, but the stored value is the MOVE rule's and GR13 holds.
